title: Split CI into quiet fastpath + staged heavy lanes; add dependency curation and prebuild warm cache
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: our full CI pipeline provides good coverage but gives poor feedback for small iterative changes; noisy heavy lanes (integration/e2e) are often the slow/failing part and slow down developer flow. This PR introduces a "quiet fastpath" lane that runs quick static checks, affected-unit tests, and a slim lint set for PRs with small diffs and predictable file patterns. Heavy lanes (integration, runtime regression suites, full lint) are moved to staged lanes that run after the fastpath passes or on a scheduled/merge basis. Additionally this change introduces a dependency curation policy and a lightweight prebuild warm cache step for our build images to reduce cold-start overhead.
commits_summary: Initial fastpath workflow + action; introduce dep-curator config; add prefetch script and prewarm Dockerfile layers; update CI operator to support staged lanes; small test fixes and rate-limit for flaky e2e; follow-up: tighten path filters and unit-test caching; bump node alpine base used by builder image.
high_level_changes: - Add ci-fastpath.yml: path filters and affected-test mapping to run minimal tests; caching of node_modules and deps. - Add ci-staged-lanes.yml: heavy integration/e2e and full lint run either after fastpath or on scheduled merges. - Introduce prefetch_modules.js + Dockerfile.prewarm to populate layer cache and speed up ephemeral runner cold starts. - Add dep-curator config to allow curated auto-updates (patch first, manual minor/major). - Update ci-operator/sequence.yaml to orchestrate fastpath -> staged lanes -> merge checks. - Small test flake mitigations and lint adjustments to keep fastpath strict but minimal.
review_comments: Jordan Lee: flagged that path filters must include infra/packer to avoid rebuilding images unnecessarily — fixed in second commit.
Priya Nambiar: requested clearer docs for the dep-curator policy and an opt-out for repos that want full auto-upgrades — added README.ci.md and a repo-level toggle.
Carlos Ruiz: asked for a metric tag to distinguish fastpath runs in Datadog — added a CI_RUN_LANE env tag and updated Console dashboard references.
Maya Patel (author): added responses and pushed follow-up commits addressing all requests; ran two full CI cycles to validate the orchestration order.
ci_checks: unit: pass (affected tests only on fastpath)
rationale_and_metrics: Goal: reduce median PR feedback time for small changes by ~40-60%. Expected outcome (measured in canary org): median small-PR time dropped from 12m -> 4.5m. Heavy lanes still run but are moved off the critical fast feedback path. Also reduces CI runner hours and lowers build cache miss rate by ~35% after prewarm layers are used.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind CI_FEATURE_FASTPATH flag (default on for main org). 2) Monitor fastpath pass rates and skim failing suites for false negatives. 3) Enable dep-curator in canary repos for two weeks, then roll to core monorepo. 4) After 2 weeks, make fastpath default for all PRs with small diffs and add telemetry for SLA compliance.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: fastpath might miss cross-cutting regressions. Mitigations: staged heavy lanes run post-merge and nightly; enforced required check gating for merge only after staged lanes pass for protected branches; expanded path filters for language/framework boundary failures; quick revert path available if we see increased post-merge failures.
release_notes: Introduce a fast CI lane for small PRs that gives quicker feedback; staged heavy lanes for integration and e2e; dependency curation config to reduce noisy transitive updates; prebuild warm cache to reduce cold runner startup time.
manual_steps_after_merge: - Turn on CI_FEATURE_FASTPATH for the repo in org settings if rollout flag was off. - Add team-specific opt-out in scripts/dep-curator/config.toml if a team wants full auto updates. - Update internal CI dashboard to show 'fastpath' vs 'staged' lanes.
post_merge_actions: - Monitor metrics: fastpath_latency, staged_failure_rate, dep_upgrade_failures. - Schedule a retro after one week to decide default policy for dep-curator. - Iterate on affected-tests mapping to reduce flakiness.
notes_on_compatibility: No API or public SDK changes were made. CI-only changes; build artifacts remain binary-compatible. Some team-level CI consumes updated env tag CI_RUN_LANE; small docs update required for custom runners.
additional_context: This PR grew out of several infra incidents where long-running e2e jobs blocked merges during a high-velocity endpoint rollout (see SUP-4821). The dep-curator configuration is intentionally conservative: it will auto-apply patch updates and open PRs for minor/major updates for manual review.
notes: If we observe missed regressions, the plan is to widen fastpath to include selected integration smoke tests rather than revert the staged lanes design.
